elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 expressly provides that “no liquidated damages … are payable by Customer,” eliminating the original late-payment liquidated-damages obligation.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 expressly provides that “no penalty [is] payable by Customer.”

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer must be an early-termination fee, with no other liquidated amount payable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no liquidated amount at all. Accordingly, it does not impose any non-termination liquidated amount and is more protective than this fallback limitation.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the supplied operative language, so the condition for applying the cap is demonstrably absent and Customer's exposure under this clause is zero.

result.reason: The redline removes the original liquidated-damages obligation and affirmatively states that neither liquidated damages nor a penalty is payable by Customer. It therefore reaches the preferred position and, because zero exposure is more protective than a capped early-termination fee, also satisfies the fallback. The retained late-payment trigger and “for each week” wording are unnecessary and slightly awkward, but they do not create a payment obligation or affect unrelated remedies.
